chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Nadr from Hisham ibn Salim and Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Ibn Mukkan, all from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him: A woman freed one-third of her servant upon her death. Is it upon her heirs to manumit her (by paying her value) if they wish, or if they refuse? He said: 'She does not have that right, but one-third belongs to her and two-thirds to the heir, so she serves according to that calculation, and she is entitled [to freedom] according to what was freed from her.'

key_terms.يُكَاتِبُوهَا: to manumit her / enter into a contract of manumission

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a servant who is partially freed in the owner's will?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of partial manumission upon death, establishing that the heir retains ownership of the remaining two-thirds and the freed portion, thereby exempting them from the obligation of *kitabah* (contractual manumission) unless they choose it. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the servant's service is proportional to the master's retained share, reflecting the practical application of inheritance and property rights in early Islamic society. This ruling underscores the flexibility in slave emancipation, allowing for a gradual transition to freedom rather than an immediate, full liberation at the owner's expense.
